topic_summary: Analysis of euthanasia policy as a contested kernel where end-of-life decision authority is read through autonomy-primary or sanctity-of-life-primary commitments. Each reading instantiates a structurally different constraint with distinct victim sets: the suffering-prolonged under sanctity frameworks versus the pressured-vulnerable under autonomy frameworks.

key_entities: Terminally ill patient (agent seeking death with dignity or preservation)
Medical authority (physician; interprets permissibility under legal/ethical framework)
State regulatory apparatus (licensing body; defines legitimate medical practice)
key_tensions: Individual autonomy vs collective protection duty (patient self-determination vs state paternalism)
Suffering relief vs life preservation (medical imperative to end suffering vs Hippocratic do-no-harm)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The end-of-life decision kernel: what grounds legitimate authority to determine when and how a life may end
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Interpretive legitimacy derives from competing moral foundations (autonomy, sanctity, dignity) embedded in medical ethics codes, constitutional rights frameworks, and religious traditions

readings.commitment: Legitimate authority derives from patient autonomy; self-determination over bodily integrity is foundational
readings.authority_grounding: Liberal rights framework; Millian harm principle; bodily autonomy as constitutional right
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: pressured-vulnerable (coercion risk from family/economic factors). Beneficiary: suffering patient. High ε from consent infrastructure requirements.

readings.commitment: Legitimate authority derives from life's intrinsic sanctity; intentional life-ending categorically impermissible
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law; Abrahamic religious traditions; vitalist medical ethics
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: suffering-prolonged (patient denied relief). Beneficiary: moral community upholding sanctity norm. Low ε from categorical prohibition.

readings.commitment: Legitimate authority balances autonomy with dignified conditions; state duty to prevent undignified deaths
readings.authority_grounding: Capabilities approach; European dignity jurisprudence; palliative care ethics
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: both suffering-prolonged AND pressured-vulnerable (dual protection failure). Moderate ε from case-by-case assessment requirements.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Autonomy reading requires accepting patient's death choice as legitimate exercise of self-determination; sanctity reading requires rejecting any intentional life-ending as categorically illegitimate regardless of consent. No single coherent framework can hold both life as inviolable AND patient sovereignty over life-termination.

axes.structural_delta: Patient autonomy grounds legitimate end-of-life authority; state permits voluntary euthanasia with consent safeguards
axes.primary_observable: Legal permissibility of physician-assisted death with documented consent; consent verification infrastructure
axes.selection_reason: Autonomy reading selected as first reading; instantiates high-ε constraint requiring consent infrastructure to separate voluntary from coerced death

axes.structural_delta: Intrinsic sanctity of life grounds legitimate end-of-life authority; state prohibits all intentional life-ending
axes.primary_observable: Legal prohibition of euthanasia; criminal penalties for physicians; palliative care availability
axes.selection_reason: Sanctity reading selected as axiom-contradictory sibling; low-ε categorical prohibition producing opposite victim set

axes.structural_delta: Human dignity balances autonomy with state duty to prevent coercion and ensure dignified conditions
axes.primary_observable: Euthanasia permitted under strict safeguards; mandatory palliative care access; independent review boards
axes.selection_reason: Dignity reading selected as third reading; hybrid framework attempting to address both victim sets simultaneously

axes.human_readable: Slippery Slope Mechanism (Normalization of Death Choice)
axes.structural_delta: Permissive policy shifts social norms such that vulnerable populations experience implicit pressure to choose death
axes.primary_observable: Demographic distribution of euthanasia uptake; socioeconomic status correlation; disability advocacy resistance
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: embedded in autonomy reading's victim set analysis; mechanism rather than independent reading

axes.structural_delta: Availability and quality of palliative care determines whether suffering-relief requires death or can be achieved through pain management
axes.primary_observable: Palliative care access rates; opioid prescription availability; hospice facility distribution
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream physical constraint affecting feasibility of sanctity/dignity positions but not a kernel reading itself

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Permissive policy shifts norms creating implicit death pressure on vulnerable populations
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Mechanism embedded within autonomy reading's victim set; not independent reading of kernel

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Palliative care infrastructure determines feasibility of suffering-relief without death
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream physical constraint affecting multiple readings but not a reading itself; omega variable for sanctity/dignity positions

omegas.description: Can consent infrastructure reliably distinguish voluntary choice from subtle economic/familial coercion? If not, autonomy reading's victim set expands unpredictably.
omegas.source: Autonomy reading victim set boundary uncertainty

omegas.description: Is unbearable suffering objectively measurable or subjectively defined? Definition determines which sanctity reading victims are 'genuinely' suffering-prolonged versus treatable through palliative care.
omegas.source: Sanctity reading victim set boundary uncertainty

omegas.description: Dignity reading requires balancing autonomy and protection but provides no algorithmic decision rule. Case-by-case assessment may collapse to either autonomy or sanctity in practice.
If universal high-quality palliative care were available, would sanctity reading's victim set (suffering-prolonged) approach zero? Physical constraint uncertainty affects reading viability.
omegas.source: Deferred axis pain_management_availability; mountain validity for sanctity position

omegas.description: Disability rights advocates contest autonomy reading's framing of 'unbearable suffering' as reinforcing ableist devaluation of disabled lives. Victim/beneficiary classification contested.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory): disability community objections absent from extraction

fracture_scan.notes: Kernel recognition confirmed: three readings instantiate genuinely different constraints with non-overlapping victim sets. Autonomy/sanctity pair meets axiom contradiction test. Dignity reading attempts synthesis but may collapse to one pole in practice (documented as omega_dignity_operationalization).
